subject: MAP: acceptance criteria and data residency/retention exceptions
messages_1_subject: MAP & security gates — evaluation plan kickoff
messages_1_body:
Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — OrbitEdge is excited to run a short evaluation of Redwood Inference. Legal and security want alignment inside a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) on SOC 2 evidence, SIG/CAIQ responses, DPA language, and data retention (logs + payloads).

High-level asks from our side: 
- Provide SOC 2 Type II report (most recent) and an inventory of controls you map to our SOC scope.
- SIG/CAIQ: will you provide an exported spreadsheet of answers or the compressed CAIQ export?
- DPA: we have a few redlines around data subject rights and cross-border transfer clauses; can your legal team accept our redline or do you prefer to exchange edits?
- Retention: Ops requires retention windows for request logs, telemetry, and model inputs. OrbitEdge baseline is 90 days for model inputs, 2 years for logs, and 7 years for audit logs unless otherwise negotiated.

We propose a 3-week evaluation window with the following milestones in the MAP: kickoff (this week), evidence intake (week 1), short functional PoC (week 2), closure & DPA sign (week 3). Can Redwood commit to surfaces below?

Please attach the MAP spreadsheet you want us to use and any current SOC2/SIG artifacts.

Thanks,
Alyssa Chang
Head of Legal Operations
OrbitEdge Inc.

---
Alyssa Chang
OrbitEdge Inc. | legal@orbitedge.com
messages_2_subject: Re: MAP & security gates — evaluation plan kickoff
messages_2_body:
Alyssa — thanks and great to hear OrbitEdge wants to move quickly. Attached is our MAP-OrbitEdge-v1.3.xlsx (MAP keeps milestones + owners), and I’ve also attached our most recent SOC2-Report-2026.pdf.

Quick clarifications / commitments from Redwood: 
- SOC 2: happy to share the full report and a short control mapping doc (included in the MAP as an evidence item).
- SIG/CAIQ: we can export a CAIQ spreadsheet; Ben will attach an export and highlight any scoped N/A answers.
- DPA: we can accept initial redlines for review. Major ask on our end: standard carveout that hosted logs used for debugging are retained per customer MAP; we try to keep default production retention conservative but will negotiate per-deal.
- Retention baseline we can commit to for the evaluation: model inputs retained 30 days (default for PoC), request logs 12 months, audit logs 3 years. We are open to specific exceptions (e.g., 90 days for inputs) but need legal signoff for anything longer than 12 months on request logs.

Proposed MAP milestone owners: 
- Evidence intake / SOC2 upload — Ben Carter (security)
- SIG export & questionnaire — Ben Carter
- DPA redline exchange — Naomi Feldman (legal)
- PoC infrastructure & data residency checks — me (Logan)

Next steps: Ben will push the CAIQ export and a short evidence checklist by EOD. Naomi will take OrbitEdge’s DPA redlines and produce an inline comment pass within 48 hours. If that timeline works, can we lock the PoC start Monday 2027-05-24?

Best,
Logan
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: MAP-OrbitEdge-v1.3.xlsx, SOC2-Report-2026.pdf

messages_3_subject: SIG export + evidence checklist for OrbitEdge PoC
messages_3_body:
Alyssa — attaching CAIQ-export.csv and a one-page evidence checklist (see Drive link in MAP). Quick notes: 
- Most CAIQ answers are completed; a small set are 'N/A' because they depend on on-prem or KMS escrow which we don’t include in hosted by default. We’ve annotated each N/A with a mitigation or roadmap.
- SOC2 items: control mappings are included in the MAP under the Evidence tab. We can also do a short control walk-through with your security team (30–45 minutes).
- Retention: for the PoC window we can push inputs retention to 60 days if OrbitEdge needs that as a test parameter. By default we keep request logs 12 months and audit logs 3 years; anything longer will need legal approval (Naomi).

I’ll schedule the control walk-through for Tue 2027-05-25 10:00 PT unless you propose alternate times.

Cheers,
Ben
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: CAIQ-export.csv
messages_4_to: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
messages_4_subject: Re: MAP & acceptance — DPA redline and retention exceptions
messages_4_body:
Thanks, Ben — the CAIQ export looks good and the control walk-through on Tue works. A few items to confirm so we can close the MAP week-of-2027-06-07:

1) DPA redline: attached DPA-redline-OrbitEdge.docx (high level changes: clearer data subject rights timelines, a clause about lawful basis for processing, and a cross-border transfer mechanism). We expect Redwood to provide an inline comment pass; if acceptable we can sign by 2027-06-03.

2) Retention exceptions: OrbitEdge can accept 12 months for request logs during evaluation, but we need 90 days for model inputs and 7 years for audit logs for production. For PoC, please confirm you will enable 60-day inputs retention (Ben offered this) and that audit logs will be retained 3 years until we finalize a production contract.

3) Evidence delivery: please upload the SOC2-Report-2026.pdf to the shared Drive link in the MAP and mark Evidence item E-01 as complete.

4) Acceptance criteria: functional PoC must run >> 1) 1k QPS sustained for the test profile (burst to 5k); 2) end-to-end latency under 350ms p50; 3) successful KV cache verification and request tracing (we'll validate a sample of 100 traces). If any of those are blocked by infra, please raise an immediate escalation.

If Redwood can meet the DPA review and the retention notes above, OrbitEdge will mark the MAP as 'Ready to Close' and legal will prepare signature pages.

Best,
Alyssa
Head of Legal Operations | OrbitEdge Inc.

Attachments: DPA-redline-OrbitEdge.docx
notes: Thread contains realistic quoting and a small forward/attachment stub. Internal participants are limited to the mailbox folder owners. Timeline and milestones are laid out in the MAP and reflect a compressed evaluation + security gate alignment.
